Vitol Holding BV Announces Major Expansion of Rotterdam Storage Facilities

Vitol Holding BV, one of the Netherlands’ leading oil and gas producers, announced plans on Thursday to invest €300 million in expanding its petroleum storage and blending operations at the Port of Rotterdam. The move comes as Vitol seeks to bolster its position in Europe’s critical energy logistics hub and capitalize on shifting global commodity flows.

The expansion project, scheduled to begin in the third quarter of 2024, will add approximately 1.2 million cubic meters of storage capacity to Vitol’s existing facilities. According to the company, this will increase its total storage footprint in Rotterdam by nearly 30%, enabling more flexible handling of crude oils, refined products, and biofuels.

“This investment reflects our confidence in Rotterdam’s future as a central node in global energy distribution,” said Jeroen Maas, Vitol’s Head of European Operations, at a press briefing. “We are responding to growing demand for secure, high-capacity storage and blending solutions as the industry transitions toward more diverse energy sources.”

Industry analysts have noted a rise in Rotterdam’s throughput of both traditional hydrocarbons and renewable fuels, with the port reporting a 4% year-on-year increase in liquid bulk volumes in 2023. The Netherlands Association of Oil Producers welcomed Vitol’s announcement, citing the importance of ongoing infrastructure development to maintain the country’s competitiveness.

“The Netherlands has long been a gateway for energy flows into Europe,” said Anna Luyten, senior analyst at the Dutch Energy Trade Forum. “Expansions like this are vital to ensure our logistics network keeps pace with evolving market needs, especially as traders seek to manage supply chain flexibility amid geopolitical uncertainties.”

Vitol indicated that the expansion will incorporate new automation and emissions monitoring technologies, aligning with local environmental regulations and the port’s sustainability goals. The company also committed to working closely with municipal authorities and the port to minimize construction disruptions.

The project is expected to create up to 200 temporary jobs during the construction phase and around 40 permanent operational roles upon completion, which is targeted for late 2026.

Shares in Vitol-linked energy infrastructure funds rose modestly after the announcement, reflecting investor optimism over increased capacity and operational efficiency. The company has not disclosed specific revenue projections related to the expansion.
